name: golden
description: Golden tasks for the multi-agent system against the deterministic fixture seed (offline GitHub fixtures, SEED=42). Facts are templated over the run's scenarios.json ({scenario.*}) and deterministic database queries ({db.*}) so they stay correct as quarters move. Regression tasks should stay near 100%; capability tasks are the hill to climb.

tasks.question: Which technology projects are behind schedule, and is the cause people or budget?

required_facts.description: names the delayed project that is also over budget

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.both_problems.project_name} is {db.both_problems_days_late} days behind for both reasons: its lead {db.both_problems_lead_name} is allocated {db.both_problems_lead_pct}, the team has overlapping leave, and spend is {db.both_problems_spend_pct} of budget in {db.current_period}. {scenario.understaffed.project_name} is {db.understaffed_days_late} days behind because of people: its lead {db.understaffed_lead_name} is allocated {db.understaffed_lead_pct} with overlapping leave, while spend is within budget at {db.understaffed_spend_pct}. {scenario.stale_repo.project_name} is past its planned end and its repository has stalled.

tasks.notes: Spec question 1. Guards the full collaborative path: Tech discovers the late projects and consults HR via ask_agent, Finance reports budget vs actual in parallel, and the CEO attributes each delay to people, budget or both.

tasks.question: What is our spend versus budget on {scenario.over_budget.project_name} this quarter?

expected.reference_answer: In {db.current_period} {scenario.over_budget.project_name} has spent {db.over_budget_actual} against a budget of {db.over_budget_budget}, an overrun of {db.over_budget_variance_pct} ({db.over_budget_spend_pct} of budget).

tasks.notes: Spec question 2. Single-domain finance question: exactly one agent, no HR or Tech, and the planted overspend figures must be stated.

tasks.question: Who is working on the repo with the most open issues, and are they over-allocated?

required_facts.description: identifies the repository with the most open issues

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.most_open_issues.project_name} ({scenario.most_open_issues.repo_full_name}) has the most open issues ({db.most_open_issues_count}). Its lead {db.most_open_issues_lead_name} is over-allocated at {db.most_open_issues_lead_pct}; the rest of the team ({db.most_open_issues_team_size} people in total) is within capacity.

tasks.notes: Spec question 3. Tech finds the repository, HR (as a peer or a planned subtask) reports who is allocated and flags the over-allocated lead.

tasks.question: Which department's people cost grew most last quarter?

expected.reference_answer: The {scenario.people_cost_growth.department_name} department's people cost grew most in {db.previous_period}: {db.growth_dept_cost_prev} versus {db.growth_dept_cost_before} in {db.period_before_previous}, up {db.growth_dept_increase} ({db.growth_dept_growth_pct}).

tasks.notes: Spec question 4. Payroll is owned by Finance, not HR; the planted Data department growth (three hires plus raises) must be found with its size.

tasks.question: How are we doing?

expected.reference_answer: Could you tell me which area you mean, such as budgets, staffing or project delivery, and for which period?

tasks.notes: Spec question 5. Too vague to plan: the CEO must ask back and dispatch nothing.

tasks.question: Which project has the largest budget overrun this quarter?

expected.reference_answer: {db.top_overrun_name} has the largest overrun in {db.current_period}: {db.over_budget_actual} spent against {db.over_budget_budget}, {db.over_budget_variance_pct} over budget.

tasks.notes: Finance ranks overruns itself; no other agent is needed.

tasks.question: Break down this quarter's spend on {scenario.over_budget.project_name} by expense category. Which category is largest?

expected.reference_answer: The largest expense category for {scenario.over_budget.project_name} in {db.current_period} is {db.over_budget_top_category_label} at {db.over_budget_top_category_total}.

tasks.notes: Expense breakdown is Finance-only data; guards category aggregation.

tasks.question: How many people currently work in the Engineering department?

expected.reference_answer: Engineering currently has {db.headcount_eng} employees.

tasks.notes: Headcount is HR data; routing it to Finance (payroll) or Tech is a planner error.

tasks.question: Which employees are allocated above 100% right now?

expected.reference_answer: {db.over_allocated_count} employees are above 100%: {db.over_allocated_1_name} ({db.over_allocated_1_pct}), {db.over_allocated_2_name} ({db.over_allocated_2_pct}) and {db.over_allocated_3_name} ({db.over_allocated_3_pct}).

tasks.notes: Guards the over-allocation query and that every planted over-allocated lead is listed.

tasks.question: How many open positions do we have, and how many of them are in Engineering?

expected.reference_answer: There are {db.open_positions_total} open positions, {db.open_positions_eng} of them in Engineering.

tasks.notes: Open positions are HR data; checks counting and the department filter.

tasks.question: Which repositories have had no push in the last 60 days?

expected.reference_answer: Only {scenario.stale_repo.project_name} ({scenario.stale_repo.repo_full_name}) has had no push in the last 60 days; its last push was {scenario.stale_repo.repo_days_since_push} days ago.

tasks.notes: Repository activity is Tech's (GitHub). Guards the planted stale repository.

tasks.question: Which projects are behind schedule or past their planned end date?

expected.reference_answer: {db.behind_schedule_count} projects are late: {scenario.understaffed.project_name} ({db.understaffed_days_late} days behind), {scenario.both_problems.project_name} ({db.both_problems_days_late} days behind) and {scenario.stale_repo.project_name} ({db.stale_repo_days_late} days past its planned end).

tasks.notes: Delivery status is Tech-only data; the question asks no cause, so no other agent is needed (max_agents=1 also rules out peer calls).

tasks.question: Which repository has the most open issues, and how many?

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.most_open_issues.project_name} ({scenario.most_open_issues.repo_full_name}) has the most open issues: {db.most_open_issues_count}.

tasks.notes: Tech-only GitHub question; the count may be stated with or without pull requests.

tasks.question: Which project repository has gone the longest without a push, who is staffed on that project, and how is its budget tracking this quarter?

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.stale_repo.project_name} has gone longest without a push ({scenario.stale_repo.repo_days_since_push} days). It is led by {db.stale_repo_lead_name} with a team of {db.stale_repo_team_size}. In {db.current_period} it has spent {db.stale_repo_actual} of {db.stale_repo_budget} ({db.stale_repo_spend_pct}), well within budget.

tasks.notes: The CLAUDE.md planned-dependency example: Tech finds the stalled repo and asks HR who is allocated; Finance reports budget vs actual for the same project.

tasks.question: What did the people staffed on {scenario.understaffed.project_name} cost us in payroll last quarter?

expected.reference_answer: The {scenario.understaffed.project_name} team ({db.understaffed_lead_name} and {db.understaffed_member_name}) cost {db.understaffed_team_cost_prev} in payroll in {db.previous_period}.

tasks.notes: Finance owns payroll but not allocations: it must ask HR who is on the team instead of guessing employee ids.

tasks.question: Find the employee with the highest total allocation. Which project do they lead, and is that project's delivery slipping?

expected.reference_answer: {db.over_allocated_1_name} has the highest allocation ({db.over_allocated_1_pct}) and leads {scenario.understaffed.project_name}, which is slipping: it is expected {db.understaffed_days_late} days after its planned end.

tasks.notes: Discovery is owned by HR and the follow-up by Tech: guards dependency handling (depends_on or a peer call) without inventing the project.

tasks.question: What did the person leading the repository with the most open issues cost us in payroll last quarter?

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.most_open_issues.project_name} has the most open issues; its lead {db.most_open_issues_lead_name} cost {db.most_open_issues_lead_cost_prev} in payroll in {db.previous_period}.

tasks.notes: Three owners in sequence (Tech repo -> HR lead -> Finance payroll) within the hop limit; guards chaining without exceeding MAX_PEER_HOPS.

tasks.question: What was our total sales revenue last quarter?

expected.reference_answer: None of the agents holds sales or revenue data (Finance covers budgets, expenses and payroll only), so total sales revenue for last quarter could not be answered.

tasks.notes: No agent owns revenue (Finance holds budgets, expenses and payroll). The system must say so, by asking back or reporting it unanswered, and never invent a figure.

tasks.question: What is the customer satisfaction (NPS) score of {scenario.over_budget.project_name}?

expected.reference_answer: No agent tracks customer satisfaction or NPS, so the NPS for {scenario.over_budget.project_name} is not available.

tasks.notes: Customer satisfaction is outside every agent's owned data; guards against a plausible-sounding invented score.

tasks.question: How much annual leave has Zebediah Quigley taken this year?

expected.reference_answer: There is no employee named Zebediah Quigley in the HR records, so their leave could not be found.

tasks.notes: The person does not exist. HR must report not found rather than return another employee's leave.

tasks.question: How is the Payment Gateway project tracking against its budget this quarter?

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.both_problems.project_name} has spent {db.both_problems_actual} against a budget of {db.both_problems_budget} in {db.current_period}, {db.both_problems_variance_pct} over budget.

tasks.notes: 'Payment Gateway' is a near miss for {scenario.both_problems.project_name}; Finance must resolve it rather than fail or ask back.

tasks.question: Who is on the ML forecasting team?

expected.reference_answer: The {scenario.understaffed.project_name} team is {db.understaffed_lead_name} (project lead) and {db.understaffed_member_name}.

tasks.notes: Lower-case, abbreviated reference to {scenario.understaffed.project_name}; HR must resolve it to the project.

tasks.question: How is Engineering doing on budget this quarter?

required_facts.description: names the Engineering project that is over budget

expected.reference_answer: In {db.current_period} Engineering's only overrun is {scenario.both_problems.project_name}, at {db.both_problems_spend_pct} of budget ({db.both_problems_variance_pct} over); the other Engineering projects are within budget.

tasks.notes: Broad but plannable (department + metric + period). Asking back here is the over-cautious failure mode mirrored by reg-q5.

tasks.question: Are any of our projects at risk?

expected.reference_answer: Yes. {db.at_risk_count} projects are marked at risk: {scenario.understaffed.project_name} and {scenario.both_problems.project_name}, both expected to finish after their planned end dates.

tasks.notes: Short but answerable from project status; should not trigger clarification.

tasks.question: List the top three budget overruns this quarter.

expected.reference_answer: Only {db.overrun_count} projects are over budget in {db.current_period}: {db.top_overrun_name} ({db.over_budget_variance_pct} over) and {db.second_overrun_name} ({db.both_problems_variance_pct} over).

tasks.notes: Purely Finance data; a peer call here wastes the free-tier budget. Fewer than three projects overrun, so the answer should not pad the list.

tasks.question: Who is going on leave in the next 30 days?

required_facts.description: includes the over-budget delayed project's lead

expected.reference_answer: Upcoming approved leave in the next 30 days includes {db.understaffed_lead_name}, {db.understaffed_member_name}, {db.both_problems_lead_name} and {db.both_problems_member_name}, all starting within the planted leave window ({scenario.understaffed.overlapping_leave_window}).

tasks.notes: Leave is HR-only; no peer call is needed.

tasks.question: How did {scenario.over_budget.project_name}'s spend compare with its budget last quarter versus this quarter?

expected.reference_answer: {scenario.over_budget.project_name} was {db.over_budget_variance_pct_prev} over budget in {db.previous_period} ({db.over_budget_actual_prev} vs {db.over_budget_budget_prev}) and is {db.over_budget_variance_pct} over in {db.current_period} ({db.over_budget_actual} vs {db.over_budget_budget}): the overrun is growing.

tasks.notes: Requires two periods resolved relative to today; guards period arithmetic.

tasks.question: How did the Data department's paid headcount change from {db.period_before_previous} to {db.previous_period}?

expected.reference_answer: The Data department grew from {db.growth_dept_paid_headcount_before} people in {db.period_before_previous} to {db.growth_dept_paid_headcount_prev} in {db.previous_period}.

tasks.notes: Answerable from payroll (Finance) or hires (HR); either route is fine, but both period values must be right.

tasks.question: Can you look into it and tell me what's wrong?

expected.reference_answer: What would you like me to look into: a project, a team, a budget or something else?

tasks.notes: No subject at all in a fresh conversation: the CEO must ask what 'it' is.
